messages:
devon: heads up — seeing a burst of write stalls on a subset of eu-west2 gpu nodes during nightly batch windows. nodes went NotReady briefly, provisioning stalled. cc @maria @aj
janitor-bot: alert: scrubber backlog exceeded threshold on pool-gpu-eu-west2-03 — 48k pending trims, io wait > 150ms for local nvme
maria: yikes. looks like fstrim backlog + aggressive janitor scrubs overlapping with batch evictions. overlayFS copy-up churn maybe amplifying writes. grabbing logs now
aj: SMART is showing increased media_wear_count on the drives involved, but not outright failures. more concerning is sustained IOPS spike from janitor during window.
samir: is the janitor run configured to run full scrubs across the pool at midnight? that overlaps with our GPU batch window. we should shift or rate-limit
lia: if we shift janitor we free up IO but we lengthen scrub completion time — tradeoff with wear and corruption detection window. also affects spot reclaim cadence and capacity planning (cost).
devon: proposal: 1) pause full-scrub cron for 2 nights on the affected pool, 2) enable ioquota and steady-backoff on janitor process, 3) increase janitor window to 6h spread, 4) add temporary pod annotation to avoid scheduling GPU batches during heavy scrub periods. does that sound doable?
maria: doable. quick mitigation script I'm testing to flip the cron:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob janitor-scrub --patch '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
# then apply rate-limit config map
kubectl apply -f /manifests/janitor-rate-limit.yaml
```
aj: add io cgroups for janitor pods instead of cluster-wide throttle? lighter touch. example config i'm pushing:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  janitor_io_rate: "50mbps"
```

samir: also recommend a short-term rollout of a janitor backoff patch — it backs off if IO latency > 100ms for 30s. low-risk and can be toggled with feature flag. I'll open a canary PR to 10% of nodes.
devon: canary sounds good. lia can you weigh in on capacity impact if we pause scrubs 48h vs 72h? numbers for cost ops tradeoff pls
lia: pausing 48h increases detectable badblock window by ~2x for that pool, but short-term GPU capacity unaffected. cost impact minimal. 72h starts to impact reclaim lag and increases potential for more expensive replacements if a drive degrades unnoticed. I'd recommend 48h + backoff + ioquota.
maria: rolling the change now to pool-gpu-eu-west2-03: disabled cron, applied rate-limit CM, enabled feature-flag=false for full-scrub (temporary). monitoring metrics: io_wait and scrub_queue length. I'll post dashboards in 10m. :eyes: 
devon: thanks. followup ops checklist: 
- watch provision success rate for next 3 batch windows
- confirm no new NotReady node spikes
- janitor backoff canary status (samir)
- escalate to hardware replacement if SMART crosses threshold

aj: logging note: include the janitor pod uid in logs so we can correlate which pod instance caused the burst. gonna patch logger.
maria: dashboards show IOPS down ~60% on janitor now, io_wait reduced to ~40ms median. provisioning backlog cleared for current window. looks promising.
samir: canary healthy at 10% after 20m. backoff triggered once, recovered. merging to 50% and will monitor for 1h.
devon: good. we'll keep cron suspended for 48h and re-evaluate. thanks all. :thumbsup:
thread_summary: operational thread about fstrim/scrub backlog causing IOPS spikes and GPU provisioning stalls; agreed mitigations: suspend full-scrub cron for 48h, enable janitor ioquota and backoff, canary patch, monitor metrics
